notSuiteTestable.req-bddo-conformance-1: Binds a SHACL validator of description graphs, not a processor of streams; the family's shape gates (test_shapes, test_vocab_shapes) apply it.
notSuiteTestable.req-hel-error-conditions-1: A processor case observes only the Processing Model category (Expression); the condition is asserted by the HEL vectors (validation/test/hel-vectors.tsv, req-hel-conformance-9).
notSuiteTestable.req-hel-ext-text-7: A statement in the processor's claims or report environment, not a result of a parse; it is checked by reading the published report.
notSuiteTestable.req-pm-alignment-padding-3: Verifying a fill byte is optional (a processor MAY compare the padding with bddo:padByte), so a case cannot tell a processor that does not verify from one that verified and agreed; the rule binds only what a verifying processor reports.

notSuiteTestable.req-core-punning-1: Whether a processor relies on a DL entailment is not observable from its output: a case cannot tell a processor that did not reason from one whose reasoning happened to agree.
notSuiteTestable.req-geometry-document-1: Binds a consumer that interprets lifted geometry; a Semantic Emitter emits the mapped ordinates unchanged, and the suite has no case format for interpretation.
notSuiteTestable.req-pm-privacy-1: The runner cannot tell a base IRI derived from the input's file name from any other base the processor reports; se-base-reported checks that the base is chosen and reported.
notSuiteTestable.req-pm-value-mapping-3: Which scales beyond -4096..4096 a processor supports is its own: no case can name a scale that every conforming processor refuses. The supported range is asserted by req-pm-value-mapping-2.
notSuiteTestable.req-raster-document-3: Binds a consumer that interprets a raster description; cell addressing is the data layout's (DLV), which the Physical Parser cases cover.
notSuiteTestable.req-spatialref-document-4: A documentation requirement on a floating-point implementation, checked by reading its documentation.

notSuiteTestable.req-hdl-modules-3: The import bounds are the compiler's own; a case would need an imported file larger than every conforming compiler's bound, and no size is.

cases.title: bddo:alignment writes fill bytes to the next multiple of the alignment
Packed decimal is written two digits to a byte, zero-padded, in the byte order in force
A negative number has no packed-decimal form
A number of more digits than the field holds is refused
The unused bits of a partial byte are written 0
A field's own bit order is the effective one, and a change of order starts a new byte
Bit fields are packed least-significant bit first under bddo:LSBFirst
A string without trimNull must be exactly its bound length
Integers are written in the effective byte order
The same description writes the other byte order for the other value
A conditional byte order is evaluated over the fields written so far
A checksum is patched after its struct is written, in the field's byte order
An unbound checksum field is computed over the covered bytes and back-patched
A bound checksum over bytes the tree determines must equal its recomputation
An outer checksum covers the patched bytes of an inner one
A layout with a chunk table is outside what this version writes
A compressed field parses back to the tree it was written from
An encoding step is encoded by its codec's contract with the step's parameters
An encode output beyond the decoded-byte limit is a resource-limit error
A length and a checksum that rest on encoded bytes are recomputed whatever the tree binds
An encoding that fills its literal region is written
An encoding longer than its literal region is refused
An encoding shorter than its literal region is refused when its codec would read the fill
A codec whose contract defines no encode direction is refused with Unsupported feature
A pipeline whose kinds do not connect is a description error, whatever the tree
An encoded struct is serialised to a fresh sub-stream, then encoded
A field whose rules all fail is written in its declared data type
A conditional data type is evaluated over the fields written so far
A node that is not of the selected type is refused
A key/value header is outside what this version writes
A text container reached through a field of a byte-level struct is refused
A tree document is outside what this version writes
An unbound count field is filled with the number of elements
A bound count that differs from the number of elements is refused
A dispatched node is serialised as the struct its key selects
A node whose members are not the selected struct's fields is refused
Fields are written in list order, a sync struct beginning with its marker
A fixed-point scale changes nothing a Writer does
A fixed-value field the tree leaves unbound is written as its constant
A tree that binds another value than the constant is refused
A bfloat16 is the sixteen high bits of the binary32 value, the infinities included
A binary32 value with low bits set has no bfloat16 form
An IBM hexadecimal float is written as the normalised number of the format
A NaN has no IBM hexadecimal form
A value whose significand the IBM format cannot carry is refused
A VAX float is written in the format's own word order
An infinity has no VAX form
A negative zero has no VAX form
An unbound length field is filled with the dependent field's byte length
A bound length that differs from its recomputation is refused
A recomputed length counts the terminator
An offset-addressed field is written at its target and the cursor restored
An offset target before the start of the stream is refused
A target already written with different bytes is refused
The padding of a bddo:padTo is its declared bddo:padByte, and 00 when none is declared
A node under a parameterised struct is serialised with the arguments its field names

A field whose presence condition is false is not written
A field bound where its presence condition is false is refused
A field whose presence condition is true is written in its place
A field unbound where its presence condition is true is refused
A region of literal size is filled to its end after a shorter value
A value longer than its region of literal size is refused
A to-end sequence that its condition ends is written as its elements, with no padding
A separated token is preceded by one space when a token precedes it
A size given by an expression is not inverted
A struct's declared size is a region, filled to its end
Fields that do not fit their struct's declared size are refused
A value in which its terminator occurs is refused
A string is encoded in its bddo:encoding
A width a bound field gives is the width to write
A Float written as text takes the canonical Float spelling; nan is followed by spaces
An infinite Float has no text-number spelling
An Integer written as text is rendered canonically and zero-padded to a literal width
A text number whose rendering does not fit its width is refused
A string longer than its fixed width is refused
A fixed-size trimNull string is followed by NUL code units to its width
A character the encoding cannot represent is refused
A tree that leaves a required field unbound is refused
A single value for a repeated field is refused
A struct node for a scalar field is refused
A tree that binds a field the description does not declare is refused
A trimNull string under a bound length is NUL-padded to that length
A value longer than its bound length is refused
